content: All HIV-infected adults and children diagnosed with active tuberculosis (TB) disease should receive appropriate treatment, regardless of their CD4 count. All infants exposed to HIV, starting from 4 to 6 weeks of age, should be monitored until HIV infection is excluded. This requires age-appropriate HIV testing to confirm the final diagnosis and the complete cessation of breastfeeding. To calculate the denominator for monitoring antiretroviral therapy (ART) coverage, review all ART register pages and focus on the specific column for the last month of the reporting period across all cohorts. If applicable, also review the list of patients who may not start ART soon after enrollment into HIV care, paying attention to the outcome and outcome date columns. Count a patient in the denominator if, during the reporting month, they have a completed antiretroviral (ARV) regimen code or if they have stopped ART but remain in care. Exclude patients classified as deceased, transferred out (TO), or lost to follow-up (LTF) by the end of the reporting period. In high-prevalence malaria or severe bacterial infection (SBI) settings, this will define the denominator. Otherwise, pull all HIV patient cards for these patients and tally all patients during the reporting period by examining visit dates within that time. For children under 5 years of age at the time of the reporting period, or those born within 5 years prior to the reporting period, include them in the tally. For patients aged 5 years or older, include those with clinical stage 3 or 4 at ART initiation, CD4 counts ≤200 cells/mm³, or specific TB statuses (e.g., positive smear results or rifampicin resistance). For HIV-exposed infants aged 4 weeks or older at the time of the reporting period, count those whose final status is not HIV-negative. Use the HEI (HIV-exposed infant) register to identify these cases. Xpert MTB/RIF results should be interpreted as follows: T: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) detected, rifampicin resistance not detected. RR: MTB detected, rifampicin resistance detected. TI: MTB detected, rifampicin resistance indeterminate. The numerator for monitoring cotrimoxazole (CTX) prophylaxis involves identifying eligible patients from the denominator and counting those who were dispensed CTX during the reporting period. For HIV-exposed infants, ensure CTX was started before 2 months of age. Disaggregate data by age groups (<2 months, <15 years, and 15+ years) when tallying the numerator and denominator. Recent evidence highlights the expanded benefits of CTX prophylaxis beyond preventing AIDS-related opportunistic infections. These benefits include reducing malaria and SBI incidence in HIV-infected adults and children, as noted in the 2016 WHO ARV guidelines. For early ART initiation in pregnant and breastfeeding women, monitor retention rates to ensure timely treatment initiation. This is critical for preventing disease progression and associated comorbidities in confirmed HIV-positive cases. For HIV-exposed infants reaching 18 months of age during the reporting period, assess their final outcome status (HIV-positive, HIV-negative, or unknown). This should be done three months after breastfeeding cessation, as per WHO guidelines. For new ART patients under 5 years of age, identify those who started ART within one month of confirmed HIV-positive status. Reconcile these cases with the HEI register to ensure accurate reporting. For TB screening coverage in HIV care, calculate the proportion of patients in HIV care who were screened for TB during the reporting period. Use HIV patient cards to identify visit dates and TB status. WHO recommends using Xpert MTB/RIF as the initial diagnostic test for all adults and children with presumed multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) or HIV-associated TB. This test provides rapid and accurate detection of TB and rifampicin resistance. For TB preventive therapy (TPT) completion, calculate the proportion of HIV-positive individuals who completed the course of TPT during the reporting period. Include patients who started TPT 12–15 months earlier and reconcile data with ART registers and HIV patient cards. For HIV-positive TB patients, monitor the proportion who start ART within 8 weeks of TB diagnosis. For those with profound immunosuppression (CD4 <50 cells/mm³), ensure ART initiation within 2 weeks of TB diagnosis. Timely ART initiation is essential to reduce high case fatality rates associated with HIV-related TB. These indicators remain a priority for countries implementing phased approaches to WHO guidelines.
